records.evidence_job: Discriminate among candidate descriptions or results to identify the one consistent with the target and the scenario evidence.
records.student_action: Read the evidence and select the physically consistent answer; distractors represent target-specific misconceptions.
records.intended_reasoning: Discriminate among candidate descriptions or results to identify the one consistent with the target and the scenario evidence.
records.student_text: A motion description says, “The backpack remains beside Ari on the seat while trees move backward past the window.” Identify the reference frame used when the backpack is described as remaining beside Ari, and cite the cue.
records.student_html:
A motion description says, “The backpack remains beside Ari on the seat while trees move backward past the window.” Identify the reference frame used when the backpack is described as remaining beside Ari, and cite the cue.

  1. the vehicle/passenger frame
  2. the trees outside
  3. the backpack itself only
  4. no reference frame is needed
records.answer: The vehicle/passenger frame; the backpack stays at a fixed position relative to the passenger/seat.
records.solution_text: A reference frame is the object or coordinate system used to judge position and motion. “Beside the passenger on the seat” fixes the backpack relative to the vehicle.
records.solution_html: A reference frame is the object or coordinate system used to judge position and motion. “Beside the passenger on the seat” fixes the backpack relative to the vehicle.

records.primary_i_can: I can explain that acceleration can involve speeding up, slowing down, or changing direction.
records.evidence_job: Discriminate among candidate descriptions or results to identify the one consistent with the target and the scenario evidence.
records.student_action: Read the evidence and select the physically consistent answer; distractors represent target-specific misconceptions.

records.student_text: A skateboarder moves east while slowing down. State the direction of the skateboarder’s velocity and acceleration, and explain why the skateboarder is accelerating even though speed decreases.
records.student_html:
A skateboarder moves east while slowing down. State the direction of the skateboarder’s velocity and acceleration, and explain why the skateboarder is accelerating even though speed decreases.

  1. Velocity and acceleration are both east because the skateboarder is moving east.
  2. Velocity is west and acceleration is east because slowing reverses velocity instantly.
  3. Acceleration is zero whenever speed decreases.
  4. Velocity is east; acceleration is west. Acceleration is any change in velocity, including a decrease in speed.
choices: Velocity and acceleration are both east because the skateboarder is moving east.
Velocity is west and acceleration is east because slowing reverses velocity instantly.
Acceleration is zero whenever speed decreases.
Velocity is east; acceleration is west. Acceleration is any change in velocity, including a decrease in speed.
records.answer: Velocity is east; acceleration is west. Acceleration is any change in velocity, including a decrease in speed.
records.solution_text: To slow an object moving east, acceleration must point opposite the velocity. A change in velocity magnitude is acceleration.
records.solution_html: To slow an object moving east, acceleration must point opposite the velocity. A change in velocity magnitude is acceleration.

records.student_text: Use the velocity–time graph to identify whether the acceleration is positive, negative, or zero and justify your answer from the graph slope.
records.student_html:
Use the velocity–time graph to identify whether the acceleration is positive, negative, or zero and justify your answer from the graph slope.

  1. zero acceleration because velocity is shown on the vertical axis
  2. positive acceleration
  3. acceleration cannot be determined from a velocity–time graph
  4. negative acceleration
choices: zero acceleration because velocity is shown on the vertical axis
acceleration cannot be determined from a velocity–time graph
records.solution_text: The slope of a velocity–time graph equals acceleration. This graph has slope -2 m/s², so the acceleration is negative acceleration.
